result.title: Convergent Performance, Divergent Mechanisms in LoRA-Adapted Vision Foundation Models for Brain MRI
result.comment: 14 pages, 6 figures, Preprint submitted to Elsevier
result.summary: Adapting Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) to medical imaging via LoRA has become standard practice, yet model selection is guided almost entirely by downstream task metrics, treating backbones with similar performance as interchangeable. We investigate whether equal performance implies equal internal representational shift. We analyse four ViT-B/16 backbones, DINOv3, SigLIP2, MerMED-FM, and BiomedCLIP, pre-trained with different objectives (self-distillation vs. contrastive vision-language) and on different data domains (natural vs. medical images). We adapt each to brain tumour segmentation and evaluate on six datasets covering both segmentation and Alzheimer's disease classification. Using attention divergence, weight-change analysis, and activation patching, we find that the four models converge to similar segmentation performance (mean Dice 78-81%) through markedly different internal dynamics, yet diverge in cross-task transfer: segmentation adaptation improves Alzheimer's disease classification for DINOv3 but degrades it for the other three backbones. We reveal a dissociation between modification magnitude and causal importance: the most heavily modified layers are not the causally relevant ones, with early-to-mid layers identified as sufficient for segmentation recovery. Restricting LoRA to these layers matches or approaches full-layer segmentation while reducing classification degradation in the three affected backbones, providing a mechanistically grounded strategy that is more parameter-efficient and more robust than standard full-layer adaptation.

AI.brief_summary: 比较 DINOv3、SigLIP2、MerMED-FM、BiomedCLIP 四个 ViT 主干经 LoRA 适配脑肿瘤分割后的内部表示变化，用注意力散度、权重变化与 activation patching 分析跨任务迁移差异，并据此将 LoRA 限制在中早期层。
AI.relevance_reason: 其 activation patching 定位与「修改幅度大≠因果重要」的分层结论，可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据的因果贡献分配与层选择性适配线索；但任务为分割/分类，未涉及 latent 推理状态的生成与使用。
